cold_open.hook: GitHub got hacked. Thousands of internal repos stolen. The company that stores everyone else's code just learned what it's like to be the victim.

markets.macro_note: Small caps leading, chip stocks flying, energy getting crushed—the rotation away from oil is real.

big_story.story_title: Something very unusual is happening with Nvidia options
big_story.angle: Nvidia options are pricing in volatility that the stock itself isn't showing—either the market is bracing for a shock or someone knows something. This is the canary in the coal mine for the entire AI trade.

quick_hits.angle: Intuit laying off 3,000 to 'refocus on AI'—the corporate equivalent of 'it's not you, it's me, and also I'm replacing you with a chatbot.'
Authentic Brands Group (Barbie, Marilyn Monroe, Muhammad Ali estates) eyeing IPO in 12 months—this is the Crocs IPO of corporate governance, and yes, it will probably work.

Eli Lilly accusing church bishops and businessmen of a Trulicity rebate fraud scheme—when your drug's rebate game is so complex that clergy are allegedly in on it, you've built a system only a cartel could love.
Lowe's beats expectations despite 'challenging housing backdrop'—translation: people are still buying stuff to fix their homes because they can't afford to move.

odd_thing.joke_angle: NanoClaw founder turned down $20M, raised $12M instead—chose the harder path with less money. Either visionary or the startup equivalent of 'no thanks, I'll walk' when offered a ride.

yesterday_callback.topic: CISA left passwords and cloud keys on the open web—the agency literally tasked with protecting critical infrastructure.
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: GitHub just got breached. CISA's still explaining how they left the keys in the ignition. The irony is so thick you could code it.

sign_off.callback_target: Nvidia options—because if those are wrong, everything else we talked about today is probably wrong too.
